english.title: Administer substance with intent to stupefy / overpower to allow sexual activity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally

(A)_[administered a substance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SUBSTANCE..), to]_
(B)_[caused a substance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SUBSTANCE..), to be taken by]_

another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE VICTIM..), knowing

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

did not consent and with the intention of stupefying or overpowering

(E)_[him]_
(F)_[her]_

so as to enable any person to engage in a sexual activity involving

(G)_[him]_
(H)_[her]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 61 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally administered a substance to OR
caused a substance to be taken by
another person knowing he/she did not consent and with the intention of stupefying/overpowering him/her
so as to enable any person to engage in a sexual activity involving him/her

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act . (Sch 3 paragraph 30).

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Ten years imprisonment

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
